title: automate-kms-hsm-tls-rotation-private-installer-helm-terraform
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Automate TLS and KMS/HSM key rotation for Private Installer, Helm charts and Terraform modules. Motivation: private deployments currently require manual steps to rotate TLS certificates and KMS/HSM keys which causes operational toil and risk during upgrades. This PR introduces an end-to-end automation flow: 1) a lightweight rotation controller added to the private-installer that orchestrates cert issuance/renewal and key rewrap operations; 2) Helm chart hooks and migration templates to ensure safe in-place upgrades with automatic certificate handoff; 3) Terraform module updates to support scheduled key rotation, CloudHSM rewrap API integration, and Vault transit/app-role wiring; 4) support for SealedSecrets controller and sealed secrets re-encryption during key swaps; 5) e2e conformance tests and upgrade/rollback smoke tests. The description below lists the changes and rollout/rollback guidance. Note: description is a single continuous string to match PR artifacts. Changes summary: added rotation-controller (private-installer/cmd/rotation-controller) which runs declarative rotation plans stored in Kubernetes CRDs; introduced a rotations/ API (CRD) with states (Pending, InProgress, RewrapKV, IssueCert, Validate, Cleanup); Helm chart changes (redwood-helm-charts/private-installer) include pre-upgrade hooks that create a Rotation CR and wait for successful validation before switching services to new certs; terraform/modules/kms now supports rotation_schedule, hsm_provider (aws-cloudhsm|azure-hsm), and adds an optional lifecycle hook to trigger rotation via the rotation-controller webhook; vault integration: terraform and installer wiring to Vault transit for envelope encryption and rewrap with HSM-backed keys; sealed secrets: added controller helper (scripts/sealed-secrets-reencrypt.sh) and helm values to toggle automatic re-encryption; docs/upgrade-private-installer.md documents the in-place upgrade path and rollback procedure. Testing: unit tests for controller state machine, integration tests that spin up a k3s cluster in CI (tests/e2e/cert-rotation) and validate cert chain swap and connection continuity; terraform module unit tests using terratest; manual runbook verified in staging. Migration strategy: default behavior is opt-in via helm value enableRotation=false to preserve current deployments; when enabled, the Helm pre-upgrade hook creates a Rotation CR to orchestrate the swap; rollback will run Helm rollback which triggers the rotation-controller to revert to previous cert bundle if validation fails; we added idempotent safeguards and tombstones to prevent key reuse. Security considerations: all rotation operations require KMS/HSM-backed keys; operator RBAC tightened; rotation-controller only accepts signed rotation plans from the control plane using the existing signing key. Performance: minimal CPU/RAM overhead; controller sleeps while waiting for operations. Implementation notes: split into small commits for review; migration compatible with Private Installer versions >= v1.6.0. Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation - [x] Helm hook & chart updates - [x] Terraform module updates - [x] SealedSecrets re-encryption helper - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Tests and CI pipeline updates

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Please add a TTL check on the issued certs to avoid double-issuing when certificate authority is slow. Response: added cert TTL sanity check in controller and unit tests (controller_test.go).

Evelyn Park: We need a clear opt-out path for existing customers; Helm values default should be false and documented. Response: set enableRotation=false by default and added docs with upgrade flags and migration steps.
Jonah Lee: Terraform change looks good but add acceptance test for HSM provider selection matrix. Response: added terratest cases for aws-cloudhsm and azure-hsm and CI matrix entry.

Security review (TBD): Ensure rotation plans are signed by control plane. Response: implemented plan signature verification using existing signing keys; added RBAC rules to limit who can create Rotation CRs.
Reviewer: CI flake on the e2e job occurred twice. Author response: increased timeout, added retry logic, and decoupled cert provisioning from DNS propagation in tests.
merge_commit_message: Automate KMS/HSM and TLS rotation for Private Installer, Helm, and Terraform (rotation-controller, helm hooks, terraform module updates, sealed-secrets re-encryption, docs, tests).
release_notes: Added rotation-controller to automate TLS and KMS/HSM key rotation for private deployments. New Helm pre-upgrade hooks, Terraform rotation_schedule and hsm_provider, Vault transit integration, SealedSecrets re-encryption helper, and documented upgrade/rollback runbook. Opt-in via enableRotation helm value.
upgrade_instructions: Default is opt-in (enableRotation=false). To enable: set helm value enableRotation=true, run helm upgrade --install with pre-upgrade hook enabled. The hook creates a Rotation CR which the controller executes. Monitor Rotation CR status and CI logs. To rollback: helm rollback triggers controller to revert to previous cert bundle; follow docs/upgrade-private-installer.md for emergency steps.
notes_for_operators: Rotation operations require KMS/HSM-backed keys and Vault connectivity. Ensure Vault transit keys are present and HSM provider credentials are configured in Terraform before enabling. Rotation controller has RBAC restrictions; only control-plane-signed plans are accepted.
testing_summary: Unit tests for controller state machine, terratest for terraform modules, e2e k3s-based integration tests for cert swap and connection continuity, manual staging verification. CI updated with e2e-cert-rotation pipeline; initial flakes addressed by timeout and retry improvements.
auditor_notes: Operations: ensure customers are notified of opt-in; Security: rotation plans must be signed; Compliance: record rotation events in audit log. Added audit events emitted by rotation-controller to existing audit pipeline.
acknowledgements: Thanks to Infra (Miguel), Security (Evelyn), and Platform QA (Jonah) for reviews and test infra support.
